title: Busy without anxiety (III.10)
hook: forty tabs, a red calendar, a tight jaw; Francis de Sales answers with a child picking berries along a hedge
tomorrow: Valeria's cleats are held together with tape. what does Sofia do?

segments.voice: Yesterday, gentleness toward yourself: correct the fault like a calm judge, and lift the heart gently. The line was gentle with yourself.

Forty tabs open. A calendar gone red. Your jaw is tight, and you can't remember when it started. Can a person be busy and not anxious? Francis de Sales answers with a picture you can almost taste. A small child walks along a hedge with a father. One hand holds tight to his. The other reaches out into the leaves, picking berries.
screen: `FORTY TABS. A RED CALENDAR.` → `BUSY AND NOT ANXIOUS?` → `A CHILD, A HEDGE, BERRIES.`

segments.voice: First, two things that look alike. Care, Francis says, is good: the work in front of us has been given to us, and it deserves diligence. Anxiety is something else, an eager, restless hurry. It clouds judgment, and work done in a rush is rarely done well. Second, a scene from Luke. Jesus says to his busy host, in the Douay-Rheims: "Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about many things." In that old English, careful means full of cares. Francis's point is that the serving wasn't the trouble; the troubled heart was. Third, back to the hedge. Hold God's hand with one hand, he says, and gather with the other, the way that child keeps hold of the father and still picks berries. And look up now and then, to see whether what you're doing pleases him. Fourth, one thing at a time. Take the tasks as they come, in order, calmly, without trying to do them all at once. A child who lets go of the hand to grab more berries may get a few more, and a scraped knee with them. Francis doesn't tell Philothea to do less. The work stays. The grip on it changes.
screen: `CARE IS GOOD, HURRY ISN'T.` · `MARTHA, MARTHA.` · `ONE HAND HELD, ONE PICKING.` · `ONE THING AT A TIME.` · then, large: `CAREFUL, NOT ANXIOUS.`

segments.voice: Rest one hand, open, on your chest or the table: that's the holding hand. With the other, do one small task slowly through the sit, folding a cloth, peeling a piece of fruit, writing one line. When your mind runs ahead, feel the resting hand and come back.
Busy without anxiety. Doing the day's work with care, one thing at a time, with one hand held.
Pocket this one: careful, not anxious, berries in one hand and the other held. Talk soon.

howItsDone: Some Catholics offer their work to God at the start of a task, or pause briefly between tasks to pray, so ordinary work becomes part of the devout life without being rushed.
